title: Customer Tier Orchestration and Adaptive Eviction Notes
body:
Purpose
---
Working notes for a practical implementation of customer-tier orchestration that ties quotas, contract SLAs, multi-region affinity, and noisy-neighbor containment into a single admission + routing story. This is intended to be an operationally simple, safe-to-roll approach we can prototype in Dedicated and then harden for Hosted.

Problem statement
---
We need a system that:
- Enforces contract-level SLOs (p99 latency, availability, throughput) for paid tiers while still allowing best-effort throughput for lower tiers.
- Prevents a noisy tenant from degrading others in the same region or on the same node pool.
- Works across regions (customer prefers region, but fallback allowed under congestion).
- Operates with a control plane API surface that product and account teams can reason about and configure.

Design principles
---
- Admission at the edge: place enforcement at the gateway layer where we have the earliest visibility (headers, org id, token). Reject or redirect before expensive runtime allocation.
- Multi-stage degradation: prefer soft mitigation first (queueing, rate shaping, degrade model variant) then hard eviction (reject).
- Telemetry-driven decisions: route/eviction logic consumes real-time signals (node-level CPU/GPU load, per-tenant token-bucket deficit, regional headroom).
- Deterministic fallback: clients observe a consistent policy (region affinity, tier fallback order) to reduce flapping.
- Operational guardrails: emergency bleed switches, per-tenant blackbox windows, and explainable metrics for SRE/CS.

Core components (high level)
---
1) Policy store (control plane)
- Stores per-org contracts: tier, committed throughput (RPS / tokens), latency SLO, allowed fallback regions, preferred model variants, preemption allowance.
- Versioned policies with rollout semantics (canary, global).
- Exposes read API to edge proxies and admission controllers (cached with TTL).

2) Admission controller (ingress)
- Fast path: check policy cache, local token buckets, and node/region headroom metrics.
- Decisions: allow, queue (short window), downgrade-to-variant, route-to-other-region, or reject.
- Emits decision metadata in request logs for post-hoc analysis.

3) Local orchestrator on serving nodes
- Implements per-tenant concurrency limits, KV cache quotas, and per-tenant memory soft-limits.
- Supports lease-based preemption: when pressure is high, leases near expiry are not renewed for best-effort tenants.

4) Telemetry & scoring pipeline
- Aggregates: per-node GPU utilization, per-tenant tail latency, per-tenant error rate, cache hit-rate, and token consumption rate.
- Produces a per-tenant dynamic "stress score" used by admission controller to compute relative eviction priority.

Routing and multi-region behavior
---
- Region affinity: default route to customer-preferred region. Policy includes a list of allowed fallback regions ordered by cost/latency preference.
- Cross-region spill: when region headroom < configured threshold, admission controller may route to next fallback region if allowed by contract and if cross-region routing latency is within tenant SLO.
- Regional fairness: we compute per-region tenant shares to avoid starving tenants in a healthy region due to spill from another region.

Quota and SLA enforcement model
---
- Two-layer quota: committed (hard) and burstable (soft).
  - Committed: guaranteed capacity for the org (token bucket refilled at committed rate). Breaching committed -> immediate rejection or controlled queuing depending on contract.
  - Burstable: bounded short-term extra capacity with decay. Used when spare capacity exists and not allocated to higher-priority tenants.
- SLA accounting: for each request we tag whether it consumed committed capacity, burst capacity, or was routed due to overflow. Automated billing/credits computed from tags.

Noisy neighbor controls (practical measures)
---
- Fast detection: contiguous rise in per-tenant stress-score + drop in neighboring tenants' tail latency triggers investigation pipeline.
- Containment strategies:
  1) Throttle at ingress per-org RPS or token rate (fast).
  2) Intra-node soft-eviction: lower-priority tenants drop into a degraded model variant (smaller seq length cap / quantized model) without being fully cut off.
  3) KV cache partitioning: limit per-tenant cache footprint; evict least-recently-used segments belonging to noisy tenant first.
  4) Proportional CPU/GPU share throttle: reduce batch sizes or increase batch wait time for noisy tenant to lower GPU occupancy.
  5) Targeted preemption: if tenant allows preemption in contract, revoke some long-lived leases.

Adaptive eviction policy (proposed algorithm sketch)
---
- Inputs: per-tenant stress_score S (0..1), committed_share C, current_usage U, region_headroom H, node_pressure P.
- Compute eviction_priority EP = w1*S + w2*(U/C) + w3*P - w4*H (weights tunable).
- Bucket tenants by EP and apply actions in tiers:
  - EP < T1: no action
  - T1 <= EP < T2: soft actions (queueing, downgrade model)
  - T2 <= EP < T3: more aggressive (throttle, KV partition)
  - EP >= T3: hard rejection / region ejection
- Ensure minimum recovery window before reversing an eviction to avoid oscillation (hysteresis).

Control plane APIs for product teams
---
- PUT /orgs/{id}/policy -> set committed throughput, allowed_fallback_regions, preemption_allowed, downgrade_variants, billing_tags
- GET /orgs/{id}/status -> current consumption, recent actions (downgrades, re-routes, rejects), stress_score
- POST /orgs/{id}/override -> temporary emergency allocation or block (SRE use)

Operational runbook highlights
---
- Alerting: trigger when region-level p95 latency > target and > 10% tenants have stress_score > 0.7 for 2m.
- Playbooks:
  - Noisy tenant suspected: enable ingress throttling and KV partitioning for top offender; notify CS for customer outreach.
  - Region-wide congestion: enable cross-region spill for permissive tenants, escalate to capacity team if > 20% spill sustained > 15m.
  - Post-mortem signals: list of evicted tenant ids, EP timeline, node pressure traces, and decision logs (must be attached to incident).

Backwards compatibility and rollout plan
---
- Phase 0: read-only policy cache deployed to edge; decision telemetry turned on (no enforcement) to collect baselines for weights and thresholds.
- Phase 1: enable soft actions (downgrade-to-variant, queueing, per-tenant rate-limits) for non-critical tiers in a canary region.
- Phase 2: enable cross-region spill and preemption for tenants that have opt-in contracts.
- Phase 3: full enforcement including hard evictions and billing integration.

Open questions & risks
---
- Billing semantics for rerouted requests: how do we credit or bill when a request consumes burst vs committed capacity in a fallback region?
- Client UX: how should we surface downgraded responses to clients (headers, structured reason)?
- Legal/regulatory: cross-region spill might violate data locality for some customers; need term in contract and runtime deny-list.
- Model quality regressions: downgraded model variant may produce different outputs—need evaluation sets and alerts tied to prompt collections.
- Oscillation risk: too-aggressive thresholds cause excessive routing churn; ensure hysteresis and cooldowns.

Next steps (actionable)
---
- Instrument policy cache reads and decision logs (owner: Liam) — 2w
- Prototype admission controller hook supporting two soft actions (queue, downgrade) behind feature flag (owner: Marisol) — 3w
- Build telemetry job to compute per-tenant stress_score in near-real-time (owner: Ethan) — 3w
- Ship internal docs for CS explaining tier fallback semantics and opt-in flow for cross-region spill (owner: Asha) — 1w
